findings.title: Shared `queued` default timestamp
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18 defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. In a dataclass the default expression is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It must use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is all sources carry a stale identical time, breaking any ordering, debugging, or expiry logic based on `queued`.

findings.title: `to_dict` not Celery/JSON serializable
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict` returns `asdict(self)` which includes the raw `datetime` object for `queued`. File src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py then puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... assignment_source_dict ...})`. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime will fail serialization or round-trip as a string that `from_dict` then stores as a str, not a datetime. Consequence is outbound sync tasks can fail to enqueue or lose type fidelity. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: Outbound assignee source param not in abstract API
findings.body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 60 calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but file src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 397 abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` is still declared as `(external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit `assignment_source`, while sibling `sync_status_outbound` was given an explicit `assignment_source` param that no caller ever passes. Any concrete integration overriding `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError on inbound-triggered assignments, and status-sync loops are left unwired. Consequence is runtime crashes for strict overrides and an inconsistent public integration API.
